_comment: PidginPharma drug interaction matrix. Curated from DDInter / standard pharmacology references for drugs on the Nigeria Essential Medicines List. severity: low | moderate | high. Loaded into memory by DocReader as an O(1) bidirectional lookup.

interactions.mechanism: Additive cardiotoxicity (QT interval prolongation) and increased risk of seizures when chloroquine and quinine are combined.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine. Use a single antimalarial regimen. If both were given, stop one and monitor ECG if available.

interactions.mechanism: Additive risk of hepatotoxicity and QT prolongation when chloroquine is combined with amodiaquine.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. Choose one antimalarial agent only.

interactions.mechanism: Both drugs prolong the QT interval; co-administration increases the risk of serious cardiac arrhythmia and seizures.
interactions.recommendation: Contraindicated in combination. Refer to a higher facility.

interactions.mechanism: Chloroquine increases digoxin serum concentrations, raising the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for digoxin toxicity (nausea, visual disturbance, slow heart rate). Consider reducing digoxin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine inhibits chloroquine metabolism, increasing chloroquine plasma levels and toxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for chloroquine side effects (itching, visual changes). Use an alternative acid suppressant if possible.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium reduce the absorption of chloroquine.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Chloroquine reduces the absorption of ampicillin, potentially reducing its efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by 2 hours or use an alternative antibiotic.

interactions.mechanism: Additive QT prolongation and increased risk of convulsions when quinine and mefloquine are combined.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine. Stop mefloquine before starting quinine.

interactions.mechanism: Additive QT interval prolongation increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmia.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible. Monitor for palpitations or fainting.

interactions.mechanism: Quinine increases digoxin plasma levels, raising the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels and for toxicity signs; reduce digoxin dose if needed.

interactions.mechanism: Nifedipine increases quinine plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of quinine toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for quinine toxicity (cinchonism: tinnitus, headache, visual disturbance).

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine reduces quinine clearance, increasing quinine plasma levels.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for quinine toxicity. Consider an alternative acid suppressant.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids delay the absorption of quinine.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Additive QT interval prolongation increases the risk of cardiac arrhythmia.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible. Monitor for palpitations.

interactions.mechanism: Both drugs can prolong the QT interval; combined use increases arrhythmia risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use an alternative antiemetic such as an antihistamine where possible.

interactions.mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing lumefantrine levels and QT prolongation risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for cardiac symptoms. Use with caution.

interactions.mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and prolongs QT; lumefantrine levels rise with increased arrhythmia risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. Choose a non-macrolide antibiotic if possible.

interactions.mechanism: Additive antifolate effect increases the risk of severe haematological toxicity (bone marrow suppression) and severe skin reactions.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. Use an alternative antibiotic.

interactions.mechanism: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine potentiates the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely and adjust warfarin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Pyrimethamine can increase phenytoin levels, raising the risk of phenytoin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for phenytoin toxicity (nystagmus, ataxia, drowsiness).

interactions.mechanism: Folic acid supplementation may reduce the efficacy of the antifolate antimalarial.
interactions.recommendation: Folic acid may be given for anaemia but monitor treatment response.

interactions.mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism, markedly increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely; reduce warfarin dose. Warn the patient about bleeding signs.

interactions.mechanism: Metronidazole increases phenytoin plasma levels, increasing the risk of phenytoin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for phenytoin toxicity and reduce dose if needed.

interactions.mechanism: Metronidazole increases carbamazepine levels, increasing the risk of toxicity (dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness).
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for carbamazepine toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Combined use increases the risk of hepatotoxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor liver function and advise the patient to report jaundice or dark urine.

interactions.mechanism: Aluminium/magnesium antacids chelate ciprofloxacin, markedly reducing its absorption and efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Give ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

interactions.mechanism: Iron salts chelate ciprofloxacin, reducing its absorption and efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Zinc reduces the absorption of ciprofloxacin.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin potentiates warfarin, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely during and after the antibiotic course.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids chelate doxycycline, reducing its absorption and efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Iron reduces doxycycline absorption and doxycycline reduces iron absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Doxycycline can enhance the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, increasing bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR and watch for bleeding signs.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids chelate tetracycline, reducing absorption and efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Iron chelates tetracycline, reducing the absorption of both drugs.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Zinc reduces tetracycline absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits warfarin metabolism, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely.

interactions.mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing carbamazepine levels and risk of toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for carbamazepine toxicity (dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness).

interactions.mechanism: Erythromycin increases digoxin absorption and levels, raising toxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for digoxin toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Clarithromycin inhibits warfarin metabolism, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely.

interactions.mechanism: Clarithromycin increases carbamazepine levels, raising the risk of toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for carbamazepine toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids reduce the peak concentration of azithromycin.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 1-2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Possible enhancement of warfarin effect; monitoring advised.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR during concurrent therapy.

interactions.mechanism: Cotrimoxazole potentiates warfarin, significantly increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely; consider reducing warfarin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Cotrimoxazole inhibits phenytoin metabolism, increasing phenytoin levels and toxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for phenytoin toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Cotrimoxazole can enhance the hypoglycaemic effect of sulfonylureas, causing hypoglycaemia.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; warn the patient about hypoglycaemia symptoms.

interactions.mechanism: Additive haematological toxicity (bone marrow suppression) when combined with zidovudine.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor full blood count.

interactions.mechanism: Additive ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity when aminoglycosides are combined with loop diuretics.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination unless essential. Monitor hearing and renal function.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs increase the nephrotoxicity risk of aminoglycosides.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol instead of NSAIDs where possible.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs increase the nephrotoxicity risk of aminoglycosides.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs during gentamicin therapy; use paracetamol.

interactions.mechanism: No clinically significant interaction; combination is commonly used. Mild additive renal monitoring advised.
interactions.recommendation: No adjustment needed; monitor renal function in the elderly.

interactions.mechanism: Chloramphenicol inhibits warfarin metabolism, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely.

interactions.mechanism: Chloramphenicol increases phenytoin levels, raising the risk of toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for phenytoin toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Chloramphenicol can enhance the hypoglycaemic effect of sulfonylureas.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin strongly induces warfarin metabolism, markedly reducing the anticoagulant effect and increasing clot risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR and increase warfarin dose as needed; re-check after stopping rifampicin.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin induces metabolism of combined oral contraceptives, reducing contraceptive efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Advise an additional contraceptive method during rifampicin therapy.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin increases steroid metabolism, reducing prednisolone efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Increase steroid dose if needed and monitor response.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin reduces sulfonylurea levels, reducing hypoglycaemic effect.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; adjust antidiabetic dose.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin reduces fluconazole levels, potentially reducing antifungal efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Consider increasing fluconazole dose and monitoring response.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin reduces nevirapine levels, risking virological failure.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination if possible; consult the ART clinic.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin reduces efavirenz levels; dose adjustment of efavirenz is required.
interactions.recommendation: Increase efavirenz dose per national TB/HIV guidelines.

interactions.mechanism: Isoniazid inhibits phenytoin metabolism, increasing phenytoin levels and toxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor phenytoin levels and for toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Isoniazid increases carbamazepine levels, raising the risk of toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for carbamazepine toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Chronic isoniazid therapy increases the risk of paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Limit paracetamol use; monitor for liver toxicity signs.

interactions.mechanism: Aluminium antacids reduce isoniazid absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 1-2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Both are hepatotoxic; combined use (standard TB regimen) requires baseline and monitoring liver function.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor liver function during TB treatment; advise the patient to report jaundice.

interactions.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects markedly increase the risk of serious bleeding.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. Use paracetamol for pain.

interactions.mechanism: Combined use increases gastrointestinal bleeding risk and ibuprofen reduces aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use paracetamol or a single agent.

interactions.mechanism: Additive gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding risk with combined NSAID use.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination of NSAIDs.

interactions.mechanism: Corticosteroids increase the gastrointestinal bleeding and ulceration risk of aspirin/NSAIDs.
interactions.recommendation: Use with gastroprotection (e.g. omeprazole) or avoid combination.

interactions.mechanism: High-dose aspirin can enhance the hypoglycaemic effect of sulfonylureas.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose.

interactions.mechanism: Aspirin displaces valproate from protein binding, increasing free valproate levels and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; monitor for valproate toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and increase the risk of renal impairment.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol instead; monitor blood pressure and renal function.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and increase nephrotoxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol instead; monitor blood pressure.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive effect of ARBs and increase the risk of renal impairment.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol instead; monitor blood pressure and renal function.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the diuretic and antihypertensive effect of furosemide and increase nephrotoxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol; monitor blood pressure, weight and renal function.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive and diuretic effect of thiazides and increase nephrotoxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol; monitor blood pressure.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the diuretic effect of spironolactone and can worsen renal function.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol; monitor renal function.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors and increase renal impairment risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol; monitor blood pressure.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs increase the bleeding risk of warfarin via platelet inhibition and GI ulceration.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use paracetamol.

interactions.mechanism: Chronic high-dose paracetamol can potentiate warfarin, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Limit paracetamol to short courses; monitor INR.

interactions.mechanism: Chronic phenytoin therapy increases the risk of paracetamol hepatotoxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Limit paracetamol use; monitor for liver toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Carbamazepine induces paracetamol metabolism, increasing the risk of hepatotoxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Limit paracetamol use; monitor for liver toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Combined use increases the risk of serotonin syndrome and lowers the seizure threshold.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; consider alternative analgesia.

interactions.mechanism: Carbamazepine reduces tramadol levels and lowers the seizure threshold.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination if possible.

interactions.mechanism: Additive central nervous system depression with increased sedation.
interactions.recommendation: Warn the patient about drowsiness; avoid driving.

interactions.mechanism: Ondansetron may reduce tramadol's analgesic effect and both lower the seizure threshold.
interactions.recommendation: Use an alternative antiemetic.

interactions.mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression.
interactions.recommendation: Use with extreme caution; monitor breathing and sedation.

interactions.mechanism: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome and CNS depression.
interactions.recommendation: Use with caution; monitor for agitation, sweating, tremor.

interactions.mechanism: ACE inhibitors combined with potassium-sparing diuretics can cause life-threatening hyperkalaemia.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; monitor serum potassium if unavoidable.

interactions.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, and added potassium raises the risk of severe hyperkalaemia.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid potassium supplements with ACE inhibitors unless prescribed and monitored.

interactions.mechanism: ACE inhibitors combined with potassium-sparing diuretics can cause life-threatening hyperkalaemia.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; monitor serum potassium if unavoidable.

interactions.mechanism: Additive hypotensive effect; may cause excessive bradycardia in susceptible patients.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure; adjust doses.

interactions.mechanism: Additive hypotensive effect and risk of excessive bradycardia.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure.

interactions.mechanism: Additive hypotensive effect and risk of excessive bradycardia.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure.

interactions.mechanism: Beta-blockers antagonise the bronchodilator effect of salbutamol and may trigger bronchospasm.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers in asthma; use cardioselective agents with caution.

interactions.mechanism: Non-selective beta-blockade antagonises salbutamol and can precipitate bronchospasm.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid propranolol in asthmatic patients.

interactions.mechanism: Beta-blockers mask the adrenergic warning signs of hypoglycaemia (tremor, palpitations), delaying recognition.
interactions.recommendation: Warn the diabetic patient that sweating remains a hypoglycaemia sign; monitor glucose.

interactions.mechanism: Beta-blockers mask hypoglycaemia warning signs in sulfonylurea users.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; educate on hypoglycaemia recognition.

interactions.mechanism: Loop diuretic-induced hypokalaemia markedly increases digoxin toxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor potassium; replace potassium if low. Watch for nausea, visual disturbance, slow heart rate.

interactions.mechanism: Thiazide-induced hypokalaemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor potassium levels.

interactions.mechanism: Spironolactone increases digoxin plasma levels, raising toxicity risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels and for toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Omeprazole may slightly increase digoxin absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels if therapy is prolonged.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids reduce digoxin absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Metoclopramide increases gut motility and can reduce digoxin absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor digoxin effect; adjust dose if needed.

interactions.mechanism: Corticosteroid-induced hypokalaemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor potassium during steroid courses.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk through platelet inhibition and GI ulceration.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs on warfarin; use paracetamol short-term.

interactions.mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits warfarin metabolism, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely; consider warfarin dose reduction.

interactions.mechanism: Carbamazepine induces warfarin metabolism, reducing anticoagulant effect.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR and adjust warfarin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Complex interaction: phenytoin both displaces and induces warfarin metabolism; INR can rise or fall.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely when starting or stopping phenytoin.

interactions.mechanism: Phenobarbitone induces warfarin metabolism, reducing anticoagulant effect.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR and adjust warfarin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Griseofulvin reduces warfarin effect through enzyme induction.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR and adjust warfarin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Miconazole (even oral gel) strongly inhibits warfarin metabolism, causing severe bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use an alternative antifungal.

interactions.mechanism: Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis in metformin users, especially on an empty stomach or with liver disease.
interactions.recommendation: Advise the patient to avoid or strictly limit alcohol.

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine increases metformin plasma levels, raising the risk of lactic acidosis.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor renal function; use an alternative acid suppressant.

interactions.mechanism: Furosemide can increase metformin plasma concentrations and impair renal function, raising lactic acidosis risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor renal function and blood glucose.

interactions.mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits sulfonylurea metabolism, increasing the risk of hypoglycaemia.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; consider reducing sulfonylurea dose.

interactions.mechanism: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, reducing the effect of antidiabetic drugs.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; adjust antidiabetic dose during steroid therapy.

interactions.mechanism: Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, increasing insulin requirements.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose; adjust insulin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding with combined steroids and NSAIDs.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use paracetamol.

interactions.mechanism: Increased GI bleeding risk with combined steroids and NSAIDs.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use paracetamol.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin reduces dexamethasone levels and efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor response; adjust steroid dose.

interactions.mechanism: Carbamazepine induces contraceptive metabolism, reducing efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Advise an additional contraceptive method.

interactions.mechanism: Complex enzyme interaction; levels of both drugs can change unpredictably.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for toxicity of both drugs when combined.

interactions.mechanism: Valproate inhibits carbamazepine metabolism while carbamazepine induces valproate metabolism; complex interaction.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor drug levels and clinical response.

interactions.mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits phenytoin metabolism, increasing phenytoin levels.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for phenytoin toxicity.

interactions.mechanism: Folic acid supplementation can lower phenytoin levels, potentially reducing seizure control.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor seizure control when giving folic acid.

interactions.mechanism: Phenobarbitone reduces contraceptive efficacy through enzyme induction.
interactions.recommendation: Advise an additional contraceptive method.

interactions.mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol; risk of coma and respiratory arrest.
interactions.recommendation: Warn the patient strictly against alcohol while taking diazepam.

interactions.mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits diazepam metabolism, increasing sedation.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for excessive sedation.

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine increases diazepam levels, increasing sedation.
interactions.recommendation: Use an alternative acid suppressant.

interactions.mechanism: Additive risk of extrapyramidal side effects (muscle stiffness, tremor, restlessness).
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; use an alternative antiemetic.

interactions.mechanism: Additive risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination where possible.

interactions.mechanism: Additive anticholinergic effects and QT prolongation risk.
interactions.recommendation: Use with caution; monitor for dry mouth, constipation, arrhythmia.

interactions.mechanism: Additive CNS depression with alcohol.
interactions.recommendation: Advise against alcohol while taking amitriptyline.

interactions.mechanism: Griseofulvin reduces contraceptive efficacy.
interactions.recommendation: Advise an additional contraceptive method.

interactions.mechanism: Efavirenz can alter warfarin levels; INR monitoring advised.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs increase the nephrotoxicity risk of tenofovir.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol instead; monitor renal function.

interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs increase the nephrotoxicity risk of tenofovir.
interactions.recommendation: Use paracetamol instead; monitor renal function.

interactions.mechanism: No clinically significant interaction; combination is commonly used for mass deworming.
interactions.recommendation: No adjustment needed.

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine increases albendazole plasma levels.
interactions.recommendation: No adjustment needed for short courses.

interactions.mechanism: Dexamethasone increases albendazole levels, which may be used therapeutically in neurocysticercosis.
interactions.recommendation: No adjustment needed for routine deworming.

interactions.mechanism: Cimetidine increases praziquantel plasma levels.
interactions.recommendation: No adjustment needed for short courses.

interactions.mechanism: Dexamethasone may reduce praziquantel levels.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor treatment response.

interactions.mechanism: Zinc and iron compete for absorption when taken together.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids reduce iron absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

interactions.mechanism: Gastric acid suppression reduces iron absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for anaemia response; consider alternate-day iron.

interactions.mechanism: Additive sedation with alcohol.
interactions.recommendation: Warn about drowsiness; avoid alcohol.

interactions.mechanism: Mild additive sedation with alcohol.
interactions.recommendation: Warn about drowsiness.

interactions.mechanism: Possible slight increase in INR with ranitidine.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR during concurrent therapy.

interactions.mechanism: Amoxicillin may reduce renal clearance of methotrexate, increasing methotrexate levels and risk of toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor for methotrexate toxicity (mouth ulcers, cytopenia) if combined; consider dose adjustment.

interactions.mechanism: Broad-spectrum penicillins can alter gut flora and vitamin K production, potentiating warfarin.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor INR closely when starting or stopping amoxicillin in a patient on warfarin.

interactions.mechanism: Allopurinol may increase the risk of amoxicillin-induced skin rash.
interactions.recommendation: Watch for rash; both drugs are commonly used together with monitoring.

interactions.mechanism: Both are structurally similar; halofantrine and lumefantrine can prolong the QT interval, increasing risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias.
interactions.recommendation: Do NOT combine halofantrine with artemether/lumefantrine or give within 1 month.

interactions.mechanism: Quinine can prolong QT interval; combined use with lumefantrine adds cardiac risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination; if quinine needed, monitor ECG and electrolytes.

interactions.mechanism: Metoclopramide may increase gastric emptying and absorption of lumefantrine; minor QT additive effect possible.
interactions.recommendation: Use with caution; separate administration by 1-2 hours if possible.

interactions.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition by ketoconazole increases lumefantrine levels, raising QT-prolongation risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid co-administration; monitor for arrhythmia if unavoidable.

interactions.mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and prolongs QT; additive risk with lumefantrine.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination where alternatives exist.

interactions.mechanism: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits warfarin metabolism and displaces it from protein binding, markedly increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid if possible; if combined, monitor INR closely and reduce warfarin dose.

interactions.mechanism: Sulfonamides displace methotrexate and reduce its renal excretion, risking severe bone marrow suppression.
interactions.recommendation: Contraindicated in most cases; use alternative antibiotic.

interactions.mechanism: Co-trimoxazole can raise serum potassium; combined with potassium-sparing diuretics (spironolactone, amiloride) risks hyperkalaemia.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor serum potassium; avoid combination in elderly or renal patients.

interactions.mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, raising theophylline levels and seizure risk.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor theophylline levels or avoid combination.

interactions.mechanism: Antacids chelate ciprofloxacin, sharply reducing its absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Give ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids, iron, or zinc.

interactions.mechanism: Iron chelates fluoroquinolones in the gut, reducing ciprofloxacin absorption by up to 50%.
interactions.recommendation: Separate by at least 2 hours; better to give iron at bedtime.

interactions.mechanism: Rifampicin strongly induces hepatic enzymes, reducing contraceptive effectiveness and risking unplanned pregnancy.
interactions.recommendation: Advise alternative contraception (e.g. injectable or barrier methods) during rifampicin therapy.
